title: Career roadmap · Audio Editor
summary: An Audio Editor cleans, edits, restores, mixes and prepares recorded sound for films, podcasts, music, advertising, television, games and digital media.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a 3-year B.Sc route, with an optional 4-year honours/research year. Build practical audio-editing experience throughout the degree through short-form projects, podcast production, film/audio post-production and studio internships.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build audio recording, editing, mixing, restoration and DAW skills; target Audio Editor, Assistant Sound Editor, Podcast Editor or Junior Audio Engineer roles.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in film/TV post-production, podcasts, music production, advertising, games, sound design or dialogue editing.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Senior Audio Editor, Sound Designer, Re-recording/Mixing Specialist, Post-Production Supervisor or Audio Lead.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine audio expertise with immersive/spatial audio, AI-assisted editing, restoration, game audio, virtual production and advanced post-production workflows.

blocks.label: Evolve/stay relevant, 2035–2046
blocks.text: Learn immersive/spatial audio, automated dialogue cleanup, AI-assisted restoration, game-audio middleware, virtual production and increasingly sophisticated loudness/delivery standards. Human judgement in editing, storytelling and sound design remains important.

items: Audio Editor / Assistant Sound Editor (0–2 years)
Sound Editor / Dialogue Editor / Audio Engineer (2–5 years)
Senior Audio Editor / Sound Designer (5–8 years)
Supervising Sound Editor / Audio Lead (8–12 years)
Post-Production Sound Supervisor / Audio Director (12–16 years)
Sound Department Head / Creative Audio Director (16+ years)

blocks.text: The senior Audio Editor should evolve from timeline-based editing into audio-production and sound-design leadership. Build expertise in immersive audio, spatial formats, AI-assisted restoration, advanced dialogue processing, game audio, virtual production and digital signal processing. Strong creative judgement and storytelling ability will remain valuable even as routine editing becomes increasingly automated.
